chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Ismail al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man divorces his wife.' He said, 'He is more rightful in revoking her as long as blood has not fallen from the third menstruation.'
ai.seo_question: When does the revocable divorce period end for a woman according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the revocable divorce period extends through the completion of the third menstrual cycle, provided the final flow is not present, thereby defining the precise boundary for the husband's right of *ruju'* (reversion). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical state of purity as the definitive marker for the end of the *iddah*, distinguishing it from mere calendar days. It highlights the practical application of Quranic verses on divorce, ensuring the woman's status remains clear for potential reconciliation or finalization of the divorce.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ishaq Bin Ammar, from Ismail Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man divorces his wife’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is more rightful with reverting back to her for as long as blood has not fallen from the third menstruation’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from ’Isma‘il al-Ju‘fiy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that a man has divorced his wife. He (the Imam) said, ‘He has the right to go back to her as long as she has not seen blood discharge because of Hayd (menses) for the third time (after divorce).”’
